messages:
oliver: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on a subset of GSP-3 machines after the recent SM capability probe tweak. KV cache hit rate drops for seq_len around 120-140 and the runtime flips to the slower kernel path. :eyes:
jun: Can you paste the profiler snapshot / microbench numbers?
oliver: Sure — quick paste from the microprof run: 
```
seq_len  chosen_kernel      p50_ms  p95_ms  kv_hit_rate
32       fast_gemm_v2       8.1     12.0    0.98
64       fast_gemm_v2      12.4     18.3    0.95
128      generic_gemm      28.7     45.2    0.62
256      generic_gemm      66.5    120.1    0.58
```
Also got a kernel switch log: "selected generic_gemm because sm_features.tensorcore_bf16=false" even though device reports bf16 supported.
matt: Huh. We added a conservative driver+SM mismatch guard (driver >= 537 && sm >= 92) that forces fallback if any BF16 probe was flaky. Could be a false negative from the probe.
carla: We saw slower throughput on SM92 hosts in staging earlier — kernel was tensorcore path but perf was worse for short seqs. Might be two separate issues (probe false negative vs short-seq kernel inefficiency).
oliver: Command I ran: `./runtest --model=gpt2-small --batch=8 --seq=128 --probe-device --collect-kv-stats`. Attached trace snippet: 
```
[run] kernel_choice: generic_gemm (reason: bf16_probe_failed)
[kv] kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.61
[latency] tokens_per_sec: 134.2
[telemetry] device_sm: 92, driver: 538.12, tc_available: true
```
jun: If the device reports tc_available:true but our probe failed, the probe logic might be too brittle (timing-based). We should add a re-probe with alternative kernel invocation and a small microbatch to confirm.
matt: Agreed. Also think about sequence-length hysteresis: currently threshold at 96, but we see strong discontinuity around 128. We could add a windowed decision that prefers fast_gemm_v2 up to 160 if kv_hit_rate>0.8.
carla: I can run a canary on 10% of SM92 hosts with that hysteresis rule. We should collect per-route p50/p95 and kv_hit separately.
runtime-bot: autotune-scan finished for host gsp-3-07: recommended rules: ["fast_gemm_v2 if seq<=64" , "fallback softened: prefer fast_gemm_v2 up to seq<=160 when kv_hit_rate>=0.85"], confidence=0.61.
jun: Proposed heuristic snippet: 
```json
{"kernel_policy":"hybrid",
 "seq_threshold":160,
 "kv_hit_min":0.85,
 "hysteresis_ms":50}
```
(we'll convert to our runtime config format)
matt: Also add a probe-retry: if probe fails but driver>=538 and reported tc_available, schedule a tiny verification kernel with batch=1,seq=8 and read perf counter. If that passes, flip flag.
carla: For rollout: canary 10% for 24h -> if p95 improves or unchanged and tokens/sec increases, expand. Rollback if p95 regresses >5%.
oliver: I'll run the verification probe + microbench across 20 hosts and upload telemetry to the perf bucket. Expect results within 3h.
jun: If we confirm probe flakiness, we should also update the unit test harness to simulate slow driver responses so it doesn't regress again.
matt: Good call. Can we also add a lightweight kv prefetch—if kv_hit_rate drops below 0.7 for seq in [96,256], attempt a kv_prefetch for next 2 tokens to smooth misses? Could recover some latency.
carla: Sounds reasonable. We'll need to measure additional GPU memory pressure.
oliver: Ok plan summary: 1) re-probe with verification kernel on suspect hosts; 2) apply temporary hysteresis policy in canary; 3) telemetry capture (kv_hit_rate, tokens/sec, kernel_choice); 4) if positive, roll to 30% then 100%. I'll post raw results in ~3h. :thumbsup:
runtime-bot: noted — creating canary rollout ticket: INF-2987 and attaching autotune snapshot.
jun: Thanks — ping me once the perf logs are uploaded and I'll run an offline autotune analysis for longer seq distributions.
carla: I'll schedule the 10% canary and add dashboards: per-host kernel_choice, kv_hit_rate, p50/p95.
matt: Leaving a TODO: revisit bf16 probe code to be idempotent and tolerant to slow compiles.
oliver: Thanks all. Will update thread with results.
